title: São Paulo: A Culinary & Cultural Odyssey: Seven days exploring Brazil's vibrant mega-city — world-class food, street art, museums & hidden neighborhoods
description: São Paulo is South America's largest city and one of the world's great food capitals. This 7-day itinerary blends iconic museums (MASP, Pinacoteca), vibrant neighborhoods (Vila Madalena, Liberdade, Jardins), legendary street food, and fine dining — all at a mid-range budget that lets you experience SP like a local.

activities.name: Arrive & Settle In
activities.description: Check into your hotel. Rest up after the flight, then head out to explore. Head to the top of one of SP's tallest buildings for panoramic city views. The Terraço Itália restaurant on the 41st floor offers drinks with a stunning sunset vista.

activities.name: Pinacoteca do Estado
activities.description: São Paulo's oldest art museum (1905) houses an exceptional collection of Brazilian art from the 19th century to contemporary works. The building itself — a stunning brick structure by Ramos de Azevedo — is worth the visit. Stroll through SP's oldest public park, right next to the Pinacoteca. Beautiful gardens and sculptures.

activities.name: Mercado Municipal (Mercadão)
activities.description: SP's legendary 1933 market. Stunning stained-glass windows and an overwhelming selection of tropical fruits, spices, dried meats, and cheeses. The famous mortadella sandwich and pastel de bacalhau are must-tries.

activities.name: Catedral da Sé
activities.description: One of the world's largest neo-Gothic churches. The cathedral's crypt contains the remains of indigenous chief Tibiriçá. Praça da Sé in front is the symbolic center of São Paulo. The literal birthplace of São Paulo — where Jesuit priests founded the city in 1554. Small museum inside.

activities.name: MASP — Museu de Arte de São Paulo
activities.description: South America's most important art museum. The brutalist building by Lina Bo Bardi is iconic — paintings displayed on glass easels create a unique 'crystal gallery' experience. Collection includes Renoir, Van Gogh, Picasso, and major Brazilian artists.

activities.name: Walk Avenida Paulista
activities.description: SP's most iconic boulevard. Walk from MASP toward Consolação — pass cultural centers (Japan House, Instituto Moreira Salles, SESC Paulista), street performers, and people-watching galore. Cross from Paulista down Rua Augusta into Jardins — SP's upscale neighborhood. Browse designer boutiques on Rua Oscar Freire, or explore the funkier Baixo Augusta strip.

activities.name: Beco do Batman (Batman Alley)
activities.description: Vila Madalena's famous open-air street art gallery. This narrow alleyway and surrounding streets are completely covered in vibrant, ever-changing murals and graffiti by local and international artists. SP's bohemian neighborhood. Browse indie art galleries, vintage shops, and vinyl record stores. Rua Aspicuelta and Rua Harmonia are the main drags.

activities.name: Pinheiros Neighborhood & Feira de Antiguidades
activities.description: Walk south into Pinheiros — more polished but equally creative. Browse the antique shops along Rua Cardeal Arcoverde. On Saturdays, the Praça Benedito Calixto antique fair is a highlight. Striking contemporary art museum with free rotating exhibitions in a colorful building. Named after the renowned Japanese-Brazilian artist.

activities.name: Craft Beer Crawl — Vila Madalena
activities.description: SP has an exploding craft beer scene. Vila Madalena's bars pour excellent local brews. Hit a few spots along Rua Aspicuelta.

activities.name: Parque Ibirapuera
activities.description: SP's Central Park — a massive green oasis designed by Oscar Niemeyer and Roberto Burle Marx. Jog the paths, rent a bike, or just soak in the scene. Home to several museums and cultural spaces. Inside Ibirapuera, MAM houses an excellent modern art collection in a Lina Bo Bardi-designed space. The sculpture garden is serene.

activities.name: Moema Neighborhood Stroll
activities.description: Walk south from the park into Moema — a leafy, upscale residential area with excellent restaurants and a village-like feel.

activities.name: Vila Olímpia Nightlife
activities.description: SP's upscale entertainment district comes alive after dark. Cocktail lounges, rooftop bars, and clubs line the streets.

activities.name: Liberdade — Japanese Quarter
activities.description: Home to the largest Japanese community outside Japan. Walk under the distinctive red torii gates, browse Asian markets, and soak in the unique blend of Japanese-Brazilian culture. The Sunday street fair (Feira da Liberdade) is a must. Fascinating museum documenting Japanese immigration to Brazil since 1908. Seven floors of artifacts, photos, and stories.

activities.name: Templo Busshinji
activities.description: The main Buddhist temple in São Paulo. A serene escape in the middle of the city, with beautiful Japanese-style architecture and peaceful gardens. Explore the concept stores and creative spaces popping up in the Liberdade-Aclimação border area. Great for unique souvenirs.

activities.name: Samba Night
activities.description: Experience live samba — SP has an incredible live music scene. Bar Samba in Vila Madalena or Traço de União in Itaim have authentic roda de samba sessions.

activities.name: Bom Retiro — Immigrant Quarter
activities.description: One of SP's most diverse neighborhoods — historically Jewish, now Korean, Bolivian, and more. Browse fabric shops, Korean BBQ spots, and street markets. Beautifully restored after a 2015 fire, this interactive museum celebrates the Portuguese language through immersive exhibits inside the gorgeous Estação da Luz building.

activities.name: Higienópolis & FAAP
activities.description: Stroll through this elegant, tree-lined neighborhood. Beautiful Art Deco and modernist architecture. Stop by Shopping Pátio Higienópolis for last-minute gifts. Return to Niemeyer's masterpiece to explore the ground-floor galleries, shops, and cafés. A fitting architectural farewell to São Paulo.
